correctness.rationale: Translation invariance on (Z/s)^n yields an explicit complete character spectrum and exact multiplicities. Strict nested monotonicity and alternating-tail estimates prove a unique threshold rho_n in (1/n,1/(n-1)); all lower Fourier sectors are positive through rho_n via a uniform finite-difference inequality. A two-symbol induced subcube plus the top-character sign excludes the entire remaining (rho_n,1). Endpoint rank follows from (s-1)^n multiplicity, with u=0 and u=1 evaluated exactly. The standalone script reproduces exact rational spectra and independent finite direct character sums, not the quantified proof.

Primary texts treat either all-bandwidth geodesic metric kernels or manifold negative-type criteria; other indexed Hamming studies treat distinct sampling, projection, or Turán problems. value.rationale: Squared intrinsic Hamming distance is not the same as a Hilbert-square distance, so radial Gaussian positivity is not automatic. The theorem gives the exact admissible positive bandwidth for every dimension and categorical alphabet, proves the surprising independence of alphabet size, and determines the full boundary nullity. This is a natural complete kernel admissibility classification with covariance and interpolation relevance rather than an arbitrary finite census.
